We could have a state multivalue that list the positions where a beam exists. It would start with state = source and we would somehow iterate over the splitter sets to see how state evolves.

There's only one problem with this: splitter is technically two levels of multivalues: multiple splitters on multiple lines. And SPL doesn't really do nested loops. (Or does it? in another challenge we do crazy things with an mvmap inside a foreach loop, but that wouldn't work here...)

The key to part 2 is to think about the problem in the right way.
In part 1, we went through each splitter, and we kept track of all the positions for the beam in state:
<ul>
• state is a list of positions where there is a beam.
• Each splitter is potentially modifying state.
• We are keeping track of the number of splits.

In other words: in part 1 we have one universe but the beam can be multiple places. In part 2, we have multiple universes, but the beam can only be in one place. This means we still only need a one-dimensional list to keep track of state:
<ul>
• state is basically a list of universes, each universe has only one beam.
• Each splitter is creating more universes.
• We are keeping track of the number of universes.

<li>And the rest is symmetrical.
